stem: Temperature is a measure of the __________ of a body.
solution: Temperature tells us how hot or cold a body is.

stem: The instrument used to measure temperature is a __________.
solution: A thermometer measures temperature.

stem: The SI unit of temperature is the __________.
solution: The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature; degree Celsius (°C) is also commonly used.

stem: The temperature at which pure water freezes at normal pressure is __________.
solution: Pure water freezes at 0 °C at normal atmospheric pressure.

stem: The temperature at which pure water boils at normal pressure is __________.
solution: Pure water boils at 100 °C at normal atmospheric pressure.

stem: The normal temperature of the healthy human body is about __________.
solution: Normal human body temperature is about 37 °C, or 98.6 °F.

stem: The type of thermometer used to measure the human body temperature is called a __________.
solution: A clinical (doctor's) thermometer is designed to measure human body temperature.

stem: The temperature range of a clinical thermometer is usually from about __________.
solution: A clinical thermometer typically reads 35 °C to 42 °C, suited to body temperature.

stem: Older clinical thermometers used a shiny liquid metal, __________, which expands on heating.
solution: Traditional thermometers used mercury, which expands on heating; many modern ones use alcohol or are digital.

stem: A clinical thermometer has a small bend (kink) near the bulb in order to __________.
options: stop the liquid from falling back quickly so the reading can be taken
solution: The kink prevents the mercury from flowing back immediately, holding the reading until it is shaken down.

stem: Before using a clinical thermometer, it should be __________.
options: cleaned and the reading shaken down below the previous value
solution: The thermometer must be cleaned and shaken (or reset) so the reading falls below the previous value before use.

stem: A laboratory thermometer typically measures temperatures in the range of about __________.
solution: A laboratory thermometer usually reads about −10 °C to 110 °C, a wider range than the clinical type.

stem: Modern digital thermometers are preferred over mercury ones mainly because mercury is __________.
options: toxic and harmful if the thermometer breaks
solution: Mercury is toxic; if a mercury thermometer breaks it poses a health hazard, so digital thermometers are safer.

stem: A thermometer works on the principle that most liquids/materials __________ on heating.
solution: Thermometers use the expansion of a liquid (or other change) with rise in temperature.

stem: The two common temperature scales are the Celsius scale and the __________ scale.
solution: Celsius (°C) and Fahrenheit (°F) are two common temperature scales.

stem: On the Fahrenheit scale, the normal human body temperature is about __________.
solution: Normal body temperature is 98.6 °F, equal to 37 °C.

stem: While reading a thermometer, the eye should be kept __________ the level of the liquid.
solution: Reading level with the liquid avoids parallax error.

stem: A clinical thermometer should NOT be __________.
options: held by the bulb or washed with hot water
solution: It should not be held by the bulb or washed with hot water, as this affects the reading and can damage it.

stem: Why can the same day feel 'hot' to one person and 'pleasant' to another using touch alone?
options: Touch gives only a rough sense; it cannot measure temperature accurately
solution: Our sense of touch is unreliable for judging temperature; a thermometer is needed for an accurate value.

stem: If you touch a metal handle and a wooden handle in the same cold room, the metal feels colder because it __________.
options: conducts heat away from your hand faster
is actually at a lower temperature
solution: Both are at the same temperature, but metal conducts heat from the hand faster, so it feels colder.

stem: A digital thermometer shows temperature as __________.
options: the height of a mercury thread only
solution: A digital thermometer displays the temperature directly as a numerical reading.

stem: The freezing point and boiling point of water are used to __________ on a thermometer scale.
solution: The freezing (0 °C) and boiling (100 °C) points of water serve as fixed reference points for the Celsius scale.

stem: To measure the temperature of hot water in a beaker, the correct choice is a __________.
solution: A laboratory thermometer covers the needed range; a clinical thermometer only reads up to ~42 °C.

stem: During a fever, the human body temperature __________.
solution: A fever is marked by body temperature rising above the normal 37 °C.

stem: Which of the following will NOT be read correctly by a clinical thermometer?
solution: A clinical thermometer only reads up to about 42 °C, so it cannot measure 100 °C boiling water.

stem: The bulb of a thermometer contains the liquid because __________.
options: it holds the liquid that expands into the thin tube on heating
solution: The bulb reservoir holds the thermometric liquid, which expands up the thin capillary tube as temperature rises.

stem: Which statement about heat and temperature is correct?
options: Temperature tells how hot a body is; heat is the energy that flows due to a temperature difference
Heat and temperature are exactly the same thing
solution: Temperature indicates hotness/coldness; heat is the energy transferred between bodies at different temperatures.

stem: A maximum–minimum thermometer is used to record the __________.
options: highest and lowest temperatures over a period
solution: A maximum–minimum thermometer records the highest and lowest temperatures reached during a period, useful in weather stations.

stem: When a thermometer is placed in hot water, the liquid column rises because the liquid __________.
solution: On heating, the liquid gains energy and expands, so the column rises.

stem: A patient's temperature is read as 40 °C. This indicates __________.
solution: 40 °C is well above the normal 37 °C, indicating a high fever.

stem: To take an accurate body temperature with a clinical thermometer, the bulb is placed __________.
options: under the tongue (or armpit) for a short time
on the forehead skin only for a second
solution: The bulb is kept under the tongue (or in the armpit) for the required time to read body temperature.

stem: Why must a single clinical thermometer be cleaned/disinfected before being used on another person?
options: To prevent the spread of infection
solution: Cleaning and disinfecting prevents transferring germs and infections between people.

stem: Which of these temperatures is the coldest?
solution: −5 °C is below the freezing point of water and is the coldest of the four.

stem: The temperature of a place recorded by weather departments is measured in the __________.
solution: Air temperature is officially measured in the shade to avoid the direct heating effect of the Sun.

stem: A rise of temperature generally causes solids, liquids and gases to __________.
solution: Most substances expand on heating and contract on cooling.

stem: The reading on a thermometer is taken when the liquid column __________.
solution: The reading is taken once the column stabilises, showing the temperature of the object.

stem: Which is the correct order of temperatures from lowest to highest?
options: Freezing water (0 °C) < body temperature (37 °C) < boiling water (100 °C)
Boiling water < body temperature < freezing water
Body temperature < freezing water < boiling water
Boiling water < freezing water < body temperature
solution: 0 °C < 37 °C < 100 °C, i.e., freezing water < body temperature < boiling water.

stem: If a mercury thermometer breaks, the spilled mercury should be __________.
options: handled carefully by an adult and cleaned up properly as it is toxic
left to evaporate in a closed room
solution: Mercury is toxic; a broken thermometer must be cleaned up carefully because mercury vapour and contact are harmful.

stem: A forehead (infrared) thermometer is convenient because it __________.
options: measures temperature without touching, reducing infection spread
solution: Infrared forehead thermometers read temperature at a distance, reducing contact and infection risk.

stem: Which quantity does a thermometer NOT measure?
solution: A thermometer measures temperature, not mass (which needs a balance).

stem: The Celsius scale is divided into how many equal parts between the freezing and boiling points of water?
solution: The Celsius scale has 100 equal divisions between 0 °C (freezing) and 100 °C (boiling).

stem: Two glasses of water, one warm and one cold, are mixed. The final temperature will be __________.
solution: Mixing warm and cold water gives a temperature in between, as heat flows from warmer to cooler water.

stem: Heat always flows from a body at __________ temperature to one at __________ temperature.
solution: Heat flows spontaneously from a hotter (higher temperature) body to a colder (lower temperature) one.

stem: A thermometer with a broken/dirty scale should be __________.
options: replaced, as accurate reading is not possible
solution: A damaged scale gives unreliable readings, so the thermometer should be replaced.

stem: The chief advantage of digital thermometers in clinics is that they are __________.
options: safe (no mercury), quick and easy to read
solution: Digital thermometers avoid toxic mercury, give quick readings and display numbers clearly.

stem: A cook checks whether milk is boiling; the most reliable measure of its temperature is a __________.
solution: A laboratory thermometer can safely read the high temperature of near-boiling milk (up to ~110 °C).

stem: A temperature of 37 °C in Fahrenheit is approximately __________.
solution: 37 °C equals about 98.6 °F, the normal human body temperature.

stem: Which instrument would be unsuitable for measuring the temperature of molten metal?
solution: A clinical thermometer reads only up to ~42 °C, far too low for molten metal; special high-temperature devices are used.

stem: As altitude increases on high mountains, water boils at a temperature __________ 100 °C.
solution: At high altitudes, lower air pressure makes water boil below 100 °C.

stem: A thermometer must be left in contact with the object long enough so that __________.
solution: The thermometer must reach the object's temperature so the reading stabilises before it is taken.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Temperature and its Measurement' is that:
options: temperature is the measure of hotness/coldness, measured accurately with a thermometer in standard units rather than by touch
touch is the most accurate way to measure temperature
all thermometers measure the same range
solution: The chapter teaches that temperature measures hotness/coldness and must be measured with a thermometer in standard units, since our sense of touch is unreliable.
